tweets.title: MASSIVE CRACK DOWN ON PAKISTANI ISI-BACKED TERROR NETWORK Union Home Minister Amit Shah said security agencies arrested 200+ operatives linked to the Pakistan-based Shahzad Bhatti Network ahead of Independence Day. According to the government, coordinated operations across 14 states led to the recovery of IEDs, grenades bearing Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, firearms and surveillance equipment. ThePrint, citing PTI and a government statement, reported that the network was allegedly involved in grenade, IED and petrol-bomb attacks, targeted killings and reconnaissance of police, defence and religious sites. Over 80 FIRs and 200+ arrests have been recorded against the network under UAPA and other laws. Source: ThePrint/PTI
tweets.content:
MASSIVE CRACK DOWN ON PAKISTANI ISI-BACKED TERROR NETWORK

Union Home Minister Amit Shah said security agencies arrested 200+ operatives linked to the Pakistan-based Shahzad Bhatti Network ahead of Independence Day.

According to the government, coordinated operations across 14 states led to the recovery of IEDs, grenades bearing Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, firearms and surveillance equipment.

ThePrint, citing PTI and a government statement, reported that the network was allegedly involved in grenade, IED and petrol-bomb attacks, targeted killings and reconnaissance of police, defence and religious sites.

Over 80 FIRs and 200+ arrests have been recorded against the network under UAPA and other laws.

Source: ThePrint/PTI

tweets.title: It was a good series, but calling it the “most accurate” is like telling the story of Operation Safed Sagar as if it was all about the MiG-21. It should’ve been called Golden Arrows or Safed Sagar ;Chapter Toni. Safed Sagar was a much bigger operation: 7,631 IAF sorties, of which 3,427 were transport sorties, the backbone of the logistics effort. 2,474 helicopter sorties, involving everything from troop/logistics support to casualty evacuation and high-risk missions. 1,730 fighter sorties and within the fast-jet missions, Mirage 2000 alone accounted for 514 sorties, over 30% of the documented squadron total. No. 7 Squadron alone flew 240 strike missions and dropped ~55 tonnes of ordnance. And I would’ve loved to see the series acknowledge Squadron Leader Rajiv Pundir, Flight Lieutenant Muhilan, Sergeant RK Sahu and Sergeant PVNR Prasad (the four air warriors of the Mi-17 crew who made the supreme sacrifice. The fighters were only one part of a much larger air campaign. No. 9 Squadron’s MiG-27MLs played a significant role. Jaguars flew too. The Canberra took a hit while conducting reconnaissance. And perhaps the quietest but most consequential player was the MiG-29, the air-superiority shield that helped ensure Pakistani F-16s stayed on the other side of the BVR equation. There were two moments in the series that gave me strong Sherdil vibes. Would you guys want me to write a detailed review as an article? What I loved about the series “Ahuja sir was celebrated and we so much needed it” So thank you @netflix
tweets.content:
It was a good series, but calling it the “most accurate” is like telling the story of Operation Safed Sagar as if it was all about the MiG-21.

It should’ve been called Golden Arrows or Safed Sagar ;Chapter Toni.

Safed Sagar was a much bigger operation:

7,631 IAF sorties, of which 3,427 were transport sorties, the backbone of the logistics effort.

2,474 helicopter sorties, involving everything from troop/logistics support to casualty evacuation and high-risk missions.

1,730 fighter sorties and within the fast-jet missions, Mirage 2000 alone accounted for 514 sorties, over 30% of the documented squadron total. No. 7 Squadron alone flew 240 strike missions and dropped ~55 tonnes of ordnance.

And I would’ve loved to see the series acknowledge Squadron Leader Rajiv Pundir, Flight Lieutenant Muhilan, Sergeant RK Sahu and Sergeant PVNR Prasad (the four air warriors of the Mi-17 crew who made the supreme sacrifice.

The fighters were only one part of a much larger air campaign.

No. 9 Squadron’s MiG-27MLs played a significant role. Jaguars flew too. The Canberra took a hit while conducting reconnaissance.

And perhaps the quietest but most consequential player was the MiG-29, the air-superiority shield that helped ensure Pakistani F-16s stayed on the other side of the BVR equation.

There were two moments in the series that gave me strong Sherdil vibes.

Would you guys want me to write a detailed review as an article? What I loved about the series “Ahuja sir was celebrated and we so much needed it”
So thank you @netflix

Daily US-Israel-Iran War Brief:
15th Aug 2026:

- We will be posting daily war updates on the ongoing war in Middle East
- ⁠Follow us for daily Brief

● Yemen’s Houthis launched an attack on the govt-controlled Mocha Port along the Red Sea coast, firing ballistic missiles & one-way attack drones at Yemeni govt positions & facilities.

● Iranian FM Araghchi said that Iran has made no decision to resume negotiations with US, and that the 60-day period in the Islamabad MoU was a window for talks rather than an extendable ceasefire.

● US Missile Defense Agency awarded Lockheed Martin a $211.4 million contract modification to manufacture & deliver additional Configuration 3 THAAD launchers for UAE under a Foreign Military Sales arrangement.

● Iran says three military pilots whose Su-24 fighter jets went down during attacks in March were captured alive by Qatari forces and have been held in the country for about six months.

● The IDF eliminated Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan, a Hezbollah battalion commander in the Radwan Force unit, following a Hezbollah terror attack against IDF soldiers operating in the Security Zone.

● A third commercial oil vessel owned by the ADNOC was intercepted and damaged by Iranian forces in the Gulf, though no crew casualties were reported.

END OF THE BRIEF

Netram Defence Review (@NetramDefence)

Daily US-Israel-Iran War Brief:
14th Aug 2026:

- We will be posting daily war updates on the ongoing war in Middle East
- ⁠Follow us for daily Brief

● US officials reported that they have received several warnings from Israel over the past year indicating that Iran intended to assassinate President Donald Trump, though US intelligence agencies could not independently verify these claims.

● US Vice President JD Vance stated that Washington is utilizing diplomatic, military, and economic tools "very selectively, very strategically" to pressure Iran, aiming to prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and to ensure the stability of global energy prices.

● US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that the US military could maintain its naval blockade of Iran "indefinitely" by rotating ships in and out of the region. Concurrently, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced plans to apply measures "never been seen" on Iran, focusing on unprecedented economic isolation and a continued blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

● US Central Command (CENTCOM) reported that as of August 12, US forces enforcing the blockade had redirected 59 commercial vessels linked to the Iranian regime, disabled three, and boarded two for inspection. Tanker-tracking companies indicated that Iran's oil exports have completely halted since the naval blockade began.

● President Donald Trump described the US naval blockade as a "steel wall," asserting that the US has full control of the Strait of Hormuz. In response, the IRGC's Persian Gulf Waterway Management Authority claimed the strait remains closed and will not reopen until Iran's conditions are accepted.

● The United Arab Emirates blamed Iran for hostile attacks on two vessels affiliated with the state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) as they transited the Strait of Hormuz, noting there were no injuries reported.

● Israel's Defense Minister clarified that Israeli forces will not withdraw from southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is completely disarmed, qualifying earlier remarks about an indefinite occupation that had drawn US criticism.

● President Trump directed future US Navy aircraft carriers to abandon advanced launch systems in favor of older, proven steam catapult technologies to address long-term shipbuilding and repair issues highlighted during the conflict.

END OF THE BRIEF
